There are far too many misinformed people who think the repeal of Glass-Steagall had anything to do with the 2008 recession.

It didn't. None of the failed/bailed out banks were the kind of combination investment/commercial banks that Glass-Steagall prohibited. If anything, the lack of Glass-Steagall helped stabilize things a bit afterwards as the banks consolidated. (You can argue either way whether or not the end result was a good thing, but the immediate result was helping to dampen the impact)

The roots of the recession really go back to the Secondary Mortgage Market Enhancement Act (During the Reagan administration), and the lack of any follow up with meaningful regulation of the ratings agencies that gave the rubber stamp allowing subprime mortgage securities to leak into the greater financial market.
